files_inspected: git log (full history, and filtered to *.py/*.cpp/Makefile)
issues_confirmed: models/linear_regression.py:29-52 - fit() silently returns NaN weights on unscaled input. X=[[1,50000],[2,60000],[3,70000],[4,80000]], y=[1,2,3,4] with defaults (lr=0.01, epochs=1000): diverges at epoch 2, gains ~8 orders of magnitude per epoch, reaches inf by ~epoch 40, then inf-inf -> nan. fit() returns normally; weights=[nan,nan]; predict(X)=[nan,nan,nan,nan]. No exception, no warning. Standard-scaling the same X fits exactly (weights=[0.559,0.559], bias=2.5), so the gradient maths is correct.

ml_math/utils.py - no loss or metric function exists anywhere in the repo. grep -rniE for mse|loss|score|accuracy|r2|metric across all .py and .cpp matches ONLY the comments at models/linear_regression.py:3-5. The MSE the README is built around is never computed, which is the root cause of the silent divergence above.

ml_math/utils.py:8 - sigmoid is the unstable 1/(1+exp(-x)) form. sigmoid(-700)=9.86e-305 but sigmoid(-710) raises OverflowError: math range error. Reachable in two lines: LogisticRegression().fit([[0,1000],[1,2000],[2,3000],[3,4000]], [0,0,1,1]) dies with OverflowError, i.e. one feature of scale 1000 is enough.

ml_math/CPP_vector.py:40-55 + cpp/vector_math.cpp:25 - out-of-bounds read. vec_arr is sized from len(vec) but C++ loops j < cols where cols=len(matrix[0]). V.matrix_vector_multiply([[0,0,1],[0,0,2]],[0.0]) -> [8.3214395e-317, 1.6642879e-316], different on the next call.

models/base.py:9 + ml_math/CPP_vector.py:40-55 - predict() before fit() returns unallocated memory instead of raising. BaseModel sets weights=[], so LinearRegression().predict([[1,2,3],[4,5,6]]) -> [2.49643184e-316, 4.9928637e-316] and a different pair of values on each subsequent call. Same for LogisticRegression.predict_proba.

ml_math/CPP_vector.py:44-48 - ragged matrices misalign silently. cols is taken from row 0 only but the flatten ignores cols. V.matrix_vector_multiply([[1,1,1],[5,5],[1,1,1]],[1,1,1]) -> [3.0, 11.0, 2.0]; correct answer is [3.0, 10.0, 3.0].

ml_math/CPP_vector.py:18-31,57-64 - dot/add/euclidean_distance size buffers as size=len(a) then (c_double*size)(*b), silently zero-padding a shorter b. V.euclidean_distance([3,4,99],[0,0]) -> 99.126. Reaches the model layer: KNN(k=1) fitted on 2-D data answers k.predict([[1.0,1.0,999.0]]) -> ['a'] with no warning.

ml_math/utils.py:10,48 - both scalers compute column statistics from the matrix they are handed and discard them, so training scaling cannot be applied to held-out data. min_max_scaler([[0],[10]]) -> [[0.0],[1.0]] and min_max_scaler([[5],[20]]) -> [[0.0],[1.0]]; under the training scale the test rows should be [[0.5],[2.0]].

.gitignore:27 + Makefile:21-25 - no tests exist. git ls-files returns 20 files and zero test files; test/ is gitignored and absent from disk; the make test target invokes five scripts that do not exist, so the command README.md:62 documents fails for everyone.

ml_math/CPP_vector.py (no __init__.py) - ml_math resolves only as an implicit namespace package, so imports work from the repo root and nowhere else. Running a script from /tmp against this repo gives ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'models'. No pyproject.toml.

README.md:41 vs measurement - the claim that distances are 'offloaded to C++ to handle larger datasets efficiently' is backwards. Re-measured at 2000x20, 20 reps: matrix_vector_multiply 0.259s vs 0.114s pure Python (2.3x slower); per-row euclidean_distance 0.530s vs 0.025s for stdlib math.dist (21x slower). Unchanged from the 2026-09-29 numbers.

models/linear_regression.py:20-24 - the except TypeError fallback does not recover. It prints a reassuring message and sets n_features=1, then dies at :36 because matrix_vector_multiply also calls len(matrix[0]). An empty X raises IndexError, which except TypeError does not catch.
models/logistic_regression.py:4 - logging imported and never used.
Makefile:11-14 + git ls-files - make rewrites cpp/libvector.so, which is git-tracked, so the first documented build command leaves the working tree dirty with an arch-specific binary.
models/knn.py:41 - predict() before fit() raises IndexError from Counter([]).most_common(1); k > len(X_train) silently uses fewer neighbours; most_common ties resolve by insertion order.

docs/kaggle-learning-notes/main_question.md:80-83 - points at kaggle_titanic/, prediction_modeling/, and research_reports/run_logs/, none of which exist in this repo; wiki/INDEX.md still names kaggle_strategies_models and lists no pages.
